slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 14:18: Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine—since he was priest of God Most High—
slides.body: “Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine—since he was priest of God Most High—”
slides.heading: Gen 14:18

slides.alt_text: Slide one introduces the proposed link between Melchizedek's bread and wine and the Last Supper.
slides.body: Melchizedek—a priest and king—brings bread and wine. Jesus later gives bread and wine as his body and covenant blood. Christians have long read the first scene as a preview of the second.
slides.heading: Did this meal predict the Last Supper?

slides.alt_text: Slide two presents the historic Christian Eucharistic typology.
slides.body: Hebrews already makes Melchizedek a model for Christ's priesthood. Early Christian writers then saw his bread and wine as Eucharistic prefiguration—a reading the Catholic Catechism preserves today.
slides.heading: The strongest Christian case

slides.alt_text: Slide three explains why the Eucharistic association is typology rather than prediction.
slides.body: Genesis says he ‘brought out’ food; it describes no sacrifice or future meal. Matthew never mentions Melchizedek—and Hebrews discusses him at length without using the bread and wine. The symbolism is historic and plausible, but retrospective.
slides.heading: A later link, not a forecast

title: Did Melchizedek foreshadow the Last Supper?
